sources.researchNote: Wikimedia Commons gives the source as Pictures and the Picturegoer of 5 June 1915 and dates the photograph itself to 1912, and its public-domain claim rests on that publication. What the file shows is not a page of the magazine but a scan of a photographic print, creased and torn across the lower left and inscribed in ink; the file supplies no photographer, studio or holder for it. The identification of the sitter is the file page’s.

media.title: Maurice Elvey — inscribed portrait, published 1915
media.description: Inscribed portrait of the director Maurice Elvey, published in the British film weekly Pictures and the Picturegoer in June 1915. Elvey directed My Song for You, the English version of Ein Lied für dich, for Gaumont British in 1934.
media.altText: A creased sepia print of a young man in rimless glasses, turned in three-quarter profile with one hand raised to his chin, in a dark jacket, white collar and bow tie, inscribed across the lower right “With my love”.
media.rightsNote: Public domain as published, following the Wikimedia Commons file: printed in an American-distributed British weekly in June 1915, long before the threshold from which copyright still runs. The object reproduced is a photographic print rather than a page of that weekly, and no photographer is named.
